project.title: The Public Theater Typographic Poster Language

why: A strong reference for using typography as the image itself: bold condensed type, sharp figure-ground contrast, and city-like pacing create posters that feel immediate without depending on complex illustration.

compositions.title: Type as the performing subject
compositions.study: Large sans-serif typography carries emotional force while image fragments provide context and tempo.
compositions.reuse: Use when a poster needs voice, urgency, and cultural confidence before image detail is read.

compositions.title: Institution identity through campaign variation
compositions.study: The theater identity stays recognizable while each production gets a distinct typographic arrangement.
compositions.reuse: Use for annual programs, performing arts calendars, or editorial series that need continuity with room for expression.

assets.notes: Condensed, stacked, and cropped type can create a loud public signal without adding decoration.
assets.reuse: Build a fresh typographic system with controlled compression, weight contrast, and axis shifts.

assets.notes: Simple image fragments support the type instead of competing with it.
assets.reuse: Use one strong supporting crop or silhouette after the type hierarchy is working.

implementation.notes: Useful for theater, festival, event, editorial, and social key-visual systems.
